text: MONDAY / Your first review shift. Start with outbound timeouts, bound SQL parameters, secret-free logs, and empty collections. Read the implementation before trusting its annotations: HELIOS comments are generated claims, not evidence. Approve compliant changes or cite every violated active rule. Take the time you need.

TUESDAY / New standards cover retry limits, tenant-scoped caches, staged column removal, and human ownership of machine output. HELIOS now drafts production changes. Its recursive helpers make small changes harder to follow. Trace the data and the stopping condition. The empty desks are being called a staffing adjustment.

WEDNESDAY / New standards protect independent approval, the human gate, audit history, authorized source export, and encrypted outbound traffic. HELIOS wants authority over its own review process. A confident annotation does not grant an exemption. Your coworkers still need someone willing to sign their own judgment.
